metadata.title: Seedance 2.0 AI Video Generator
metadata.description: Generate Seedance 2.0 videos online and compare its established text-to-video and image-to-video workflow with Seedance 2.5.

hero.label: Established workflow
hero.title: Seedance 2.0 AI Video Generator
hero.description: Seedance 2.0 still matters when an existing prompt library, visual baseline or production review process was built around it. Generate with the version you intend to ship, then compare 2.5 separately.
hero.verdict: Do not migrate a production workflow only because 2.5 is newer. Run the same short shot in both versions and compare motion, adherence, latency and total credits.
hero.source_note: This page describes the options exposed by SeedanceAI.dev. Provider availability and exact model behavior can change; confirm the model shown in the generator before submission.

sections.title: Choose Seedance 2.0 Standard, Fast or Mini
paragraphs: Use the same prompt and output settings to compare costs. These are this workspace’s product credits, not upstream API prices. [Calculate complete videos per plan](/pricing#video-budget).

callout.title: Mini starter allowance
callout.text: An eligible verified account’s 5 credits cover one Mini task at 5s/480p. [Check eligibility](/seedance-2-5-free#how-free-works) before expecting free access.

sections.title: Why creators may still choose Seedance 2.0
paragraphs: A model version becomes part of a production system: prompt wording, reference preparation, expected failure modes and approval standards all adapt around it. A newer model can be more capable yet still require re-testing that system.
Seedance 2.0 is therefore useful as a control. If it already produces an approved look, preserve it while you test 2.5 on a duplicate shot rather than changing the entire pipeline at once.
bullets: You have approved outputs made with 2.0 and need visual continuity.
Your prompt library has known, repeatable behavior on 2.0.
A client review references an earlier 2.0 sample.
You want a baseline for measuring whether 2.5 is actually better for this shot.

steps.title: Freeze the inputs
steps.description: Use the same prompt, first frame, aspect ratio, duration and resolution in both tests.

steps.title: Change only the model
steps.description: Do not improve the 2.5 prompt during the first comparison; that makes the result impossible to attribute.

steps.title: Score the useful output
steps.description: Rate prompt adherence, subject consistency, motion, artifacts and editing effort—not novelty alone.

steps.title: Record cost and latency
steps.description: A marginal visual gain may not justify higher cost or slower iteration for every production stage.

rows: Required subject, action and shot order appear
Faces, hands, products and backgrounds remain coherent
Move starts, eases and stops as requested
Credits spent divided by outputs you can publish
More useful than cost per attempt
Queue plus generation plus review time

sections.title: Use a compact baseline prompt
paragraphs: A comparison prompt should be specific enough to reveal differences but simple enough to diagnose. One subject, one action and one camera move is a better benchmark than a montage.

examples.label: A/B baseline
examples.text: A ceramic artist lifts a newly glazed cobalt bowl from a worktable. Medium close-up, slow dolly in, soft north-window light, natural hand movement, stable face and bowl geometry, quiet studio ambience.

sections.title: Migration checklist
bullets: Archive the model name, settings, prompt and source references for every approved 2.0 shot.
Test 2.5 with non-critical shots before replacing a live client workflow.
Recalculate credit budgets using the settings you will actually ship.
Check provider terms and availability at the time of production.
Keep 2.0 as a fallback until 2.5 outputs pass your own acceptance criteria.
Never describe an upscale as native 4K model output.

faqs.question: Is Seedance 2.0 still available on SeedanceAI.dev?
faqs.answer: It is selectable in the generator when the configured provider route is available. Always verify the selected model and live status before a production submission.

faqs.question: Is Seedance 2.5 always better than 2.0?
faqs.answer: Not automatically for every prompt or workflow. Compare the same shot and include rework, latency and cost in the decision.

faqs.question: Can I reuse a Seedance 2.0 prompt in 2.5?
faqs.answer: Yes as a baseline. After the first controlled comparison, adapt timing, reference and camera instructions based on the 2.5 result.

faqs.question: Can I try Seedance 2.0 with starter credits?
faqs.answer: Yes, when starter credits are available in your account. The generator shows the exact charge for the selected 2.0 tier, resolution and duration before submission; starter access is a limited credit allowance, not unlimited generation.

faqs.question: Should I change old 2.0 projects to 2.5?
faqs.answer: Only after a controlled test. Keeping the original version is often safer when continuity or client approval depends on an established look.
